gp.heading: Cost of Goods Sold & Gross Profit
gp.text:
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, our cost of goods sold was $8,986,728 compared to $1,294,200 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $7,692,528 or 594%. Cost of goods sold primarily relate to product costs from our sales, but also include certain shipping and other direct and indirect product costs. The increase in cost of goods sold is driven entirely by the increase in our revenue.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, our gross profit was $4,916,304 compared to $840,388 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $4,075,916 or 485%. Our gross margin, as a percentage of sales, totaled 35.47% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to gross margin of approximately 39.4% during the three months ended September 30, 2025. Our gross profit is entirely driven based on our growth in top line revenue, while the decrease in margins is driven primarily by our continued and rapid expansion of manufacturing, however, we believe our margins are still within normal operating limits and will continue to increase as our manufacturing process continues to mature.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, operations expenses totaled $2,012,744 compared to $636,705 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $1,376,039 or 216%. Operations expense relate to expenses incurred for fulfilling orders and warehouse related expenditures including our warehouse personnel, supplies, and shipping expenses. The increase primarily relates to additional costs incurred related to our motor factory operations that we are putting in place along with additional shipping costs from the increase in revenue.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, research and development expenses totaled $350,548 compared to $39,369 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $311,179 or 790%. Research and development expense primarily relates to new product development and is subject to fluctuations based on specific research and development projects ongoing during the period and include both internal and external resources and costs associated with new product development.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, sales and marketing expenses totaled $613,614 compared to $373,539 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $240,075 or 64%.

sm.text: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, sales and marketing expenses totaled $613,614 compared to $373,539 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase of $240,075 or 64%. The increase primarily relates to the buildout of our sales and marketing teams as our business shifts from retail to enterprise. In addition, we incurred additional expenses during the second quarter related to marketing events and increase in ad spend during the period.

ga.text: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, general and administrative expenses totaled $10,238,161 compared to $4,730,063 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $5,508,098 or 116%. General and administrative expenses include expenses related to operating as a public company, including legal, auditing and other professional fees, public company insurance expense, investor relations and other costs associated with being public. We have also increased our headcount to support our growth, including expanding our accounting, HR, and facilities staff. We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase as we continue to increase our infrastructure with additional hires, systems and processes, and as we become subject to additional compliance related activities. We also anticipate professional fees and other expenses related to being a public company to increase. In addition, we anticipate our non-cash stock compensation expense to be higher in 2026. We do not anticipate our general and administrative expenses to increase at the same rate as our revenue as we start to gain operational efficiencies at scale.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, other income and expense totaled other expense of $16,681,327 compared to other income of $6,565,202 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in a decrease of $23,246,529. This decrease relates primarily to our unrealized loss from short-term investments of $24,231,394 offset by an increase in interest income increase of $985,489.

net.heading: Net Income (Loss)
net.text: Our net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026, totaled $25,044,948 compared to a net income of $1,603,465 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in an increase in net loss of $26,648,413 or 1,661%. This increase in net loss primarily relates to the increase in unrealized loss from trading securities of $24,231,394.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $73,554,146 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net cash used in operating activities of $11,394,294 during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $62,159,852 or 545%. The increase was primarily attributable to changes in working capital, including increase in inventory of $35,559,329, prepaid and deposits for inventory of $7,493,589, accounts receivable of $16,801,237, and offset by an increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses of $4,142,716, and an increase in operating lease liabilities of $1,164,495. The Company recorded unrealized loss on short term investments of $12,773,139 and realized gains of $9,532,673.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, we had current assets totaling $351,312,208 primarily consisting of cash balances of $161,965,505, short-term investments of $98,391,766, accounts receivable of $18,703,356, inventory of $42,622,077, other current assets of $1,370,481 and deposits for inventory of $23,259,023. As of September 30, 2026, our current liabilities totaled $10,142,634 and consisted primarily of accounts payable and accrued expenses of $6,055,909, deferred revenue of $114,491, the current portion of operating lease liabilities of $972,234, and contingent consideration of $3,000,000 related to the Rotor Lab acquisition. Our net working capital as of September 30, 2026 was $336,169,577.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities was $68,906,754 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to net cash used in investing activities of $12,457,633 during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $56,449,121. This increase consisted of $82,499,998 used in our strategic short-term investments, $6,295,729 in purchases of property and equipment, partially offset by proceeds from sales of short term investments of $20,082,674.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: During the three months ended September 30, 2026 we generated revenues totaling $13,903,032 compared to $2,134,588 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $11,768,444 or 551%. The increase in revenue primarily relates to the increase and establishment of our enterprise business and revenue related to our National Defense Authorization Act (“NDAA”) and Blue UAS products. Our enterprise revenue was $12,556,925 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $976,138 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. We started manufacturing production on certain products including drone motors, headsets, cameras and other drone related products during 2026. As we continue to expand our manufacturing capabilities and the larger drone market develops, we continue to see significant increased interest and demand in our manufactured products in the fourth quarter. We expect our revenue to continue to grow as we continue to build out our capacity including our manufacturing facilities and products and significantly increasing our manufacturing staff to handle additional demand from the market. With the acquisition of Upgrade Energy and the opening of our new Orlando battery manufacturing facility, we see battery manufacturing being a key part of the total mix of sales.

intro.text: Unusual Machines manufactures and sells drone components and drones across a diversified brand portfolio, which includes Fat Shark, the leader in FPV (first-person view) ultra-low-latency video goggles for drone pilots. The Company also retails small, acrobatic FPV drones and equipment directly to consumers through the curated Rotor Riot ecommerce store. With a changing regulatory environment, Unusual Machines seeks to be a dominant Tier-1 parts supplier to the fast-growing, multi-billion-dollar U.S. drone industry. According to Fact.MR, the global drone accessories market is currently valued at $25.2 billion and is set to reach $156 billion by 2034. For more information, please visit unusualmachines.com.

s.t: Specifically, in Europe and the United Kingdom, companies may face temporary or definitive bans on data processing and other corrective actions including fines of up to €20 million under the EU GDPR, £17.5 million under the UK GDPR or, in each case, 4% of annual global revenue, whichever is greater or private litigation related to processing of personal data brought by classes of data subjects or consumer protection organizations authorized at law to represent their interests.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, Customer A and Customer B accounted for approximately 16.7 % and 15.9 % of the Company’s total revenues, respectively.
Customer A did no t have any outstanding accounts receivable as of December 31, 2025, and Customer B had approximately 62.6 % of the total accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2025.
Therefore, you should not rely on any of these forward-looking statements.

Our ability to meet customers’ demands depends, in part, on its ability to obtain timely and adequate delivery of high-quality materials, components and subsystems, many of which are obtained from a select group of specialized suppliers, including some sole-source providers.
In order to mitigate potential disruptions, we maintain long-term, non-binding agreements with several key suppliers that help stabilize pricing, reduce lead times and enhance planning accuracy.
Additionally, credit constraints among key suppliers could impact our cash flow.

Our future growth depends on increasing manufacturing capacity of its products, and any failure to adequately increase such capacity could have a material adverse impact on our business and operating results.
Because we rely on a limited number of suppliers, for our component parts our business may be adversely affected .
The drone industry relies on limited sources to supply certain components and materials used in the manufacturing of drone components.

Our reliance on a small number of suppliers involves a number of additional risks, including risks related to supplier capacity constraints, price increases, timely delivery, component quality, failure of a key supplier to remain in business and adjust to market conditions, delays in, or the inability to execute on, a supplier roadmap for components and technologies; and natural disasters, fire, acts of terrorism or other catastrophic events, including global pandemics.

Fat Shark and Rotor Riot rely on third party suppliers for the resources needed to navigate these processes and expect to continue to rely on such parties when we manufacture and market our component parts.
Our products, including motors, batteries, and other advanced components, rely on rare earth metals for their manufacturing, of which a significant majority are sourced from China.

If our facilities and information technology systems or those of our key suppliers are damaged as a result of disasters or unpredictable events, it could have an adverse effect on our business operations.
